To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the gene expression profile in GBCs changes during postnatal development; 2) most of these changes are not related to the maturation of synaptic function; 3) changes in the expression levels of voltage‐gated channels and calcium‐buffering proteins are important for defining the key functional properties of the mature calyx.
the maturation of the auditory brainstem synapse, the calyx of held, is accompanied by a large change in the expression of genes that encode proteins involved in synaptic function.

the expression of genes implicated in the synaptic vesicular cycle, ion channels and calcium homeostasis is regulated during the functional maturation of the central synapse, the calyx of held, in the mouse auditory system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the maturation of the auditory system.
the molecular mechanisms of synaptic maturation.
the molecular basis of functional maturation of synapses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the calyx of held undergoes a massive reorganization during the maturation period, with a strong increase in the expression of genes related to ion channel and synaptic vesicle trafficking, as well as genes implicated in general neuronal function.
the gene expression profile during maturation of a synapse is not only driven by the need for a mature functional synapse but also reflects the general maturation of the neuron.
the gene expression profile is not a good predictor of the gene expression profile.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the maturation of the GBCs and their calyx of Held synapse involves changes in the expression of many different genes, and that these changes are mostly related to the general cell biology, rather than synaptic function.

the expression of ion channels, calcium‐binding proteins and other proteins involved in synaptic function are strongly regulated during the maturation of the auditory brainstem, whereas the expression of most genes implicated in the synaptic vesicles cycle is only moderately regulated.

the maturation of the auditory system is characterized by the regulation of genes involved in the general cell and synaptic physiology of GBCs, and by the strong regulation of genes related to the control of the presynaptic calcium concentration.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the central nervous system, maturation of a given synaptic connection is associated with a general upregulation of genes involved in the general cell physiology of the neuron, while the regulation of genes involved in synaptic transmission is restricted to the onset of hearing.
the gene expression profile is not a static feature of a synapse, but is rather dynamic and changes during the maturation of the synapse.
the maturation of the auditory system involves changes in the expression of many genes.
